marks.gloss_en: תניא נמי הכי: (קנים של) דוקרנין מסככין בהן
the baraita as worded: reeds and spades (dukranin) may be used for roofing
דתנן: מצות אזוב שלשה קלחים ... רבי יוסי אומר ... ושייריו שנים (bare דתנן; kind tanya_kevatei is the corpus's kind for a bare citation formula)
Rav Chisda: binding three is called a binding
והתניא: תחילתו שנים ושייריו אחד כשר -- an anonymous baraita with two sufficing, i.e. the Rabbis' three is only for the mitzva
the baraita: hyssop beginning with two and remaining one is valid
מיתיבי: hyssop -- not any hyssop with a modifying name; so 'bitter herbs of the marsh', a modified name, should not qualify
hyssop -- and not Greek, stibium, desert or Roman hyssop, nor any hyssop with a modifying name
a modifying name is one differentiated before Sinai; bitter herbs were never so differentiated (= p_abaye_shem_levai, p_merarita_lo_nishtana)
Abaye: whatever had its name differentiated before the giving of the Torah, and the Torah was particular about it -- that is known to have a modifying name
their name is plain bitter herbs; 'of the marsh' only says where they grow (= p_rava_merarita_stam)
Rava: their name is plain 'bitter herbs'; they are called 'of the marsh' only because they are found in the marsh
והתניא רבי יוסי אומר: two-and-one invalid, valid only three-and-two -- so R' Yosei's three is indispensable; the mapping is reversed (איפוך)
R' Yosei (baraita): hyssop beginning with two and remaining one is invalid; it is valid only beginning with three and remaining two
שייריו אחד פסול? הא אמרת שייריו אחד כשר! -- the seifa implies remnants of one are invalid, against the reisha
the reason: since their smell turns foul, one abandons the sukkah and leaves
one may roof with thorns
one may roof with the palm's offshoot (branches growing from one stem)
one may roof with reed offshoots
with the bitter herbs of the marsh a person fulfils his Passover obligation
three stalks are required only for the mitzva ab initio; two suffice after the fact
